meta.title: Gentle Strength & Swim Plan
meta.purpose: Build sustainable strength, core stability, general fitness and confidence while working with variable pain and fatigue.
principles: Respect your body's limits on the day
meta.disclaimer: This app is a personal exercise log, not medical advice. Check with your GP or physio before starting or changing exercise, and ask a gym instructor to check machine setup.

rules: This is a flexible target, not a weekly quota.
Add recovery days whenever you need them.
Missed sessions are not made up.
Reduce or rearrange activity if sessions feel too close together.
Don't increase swim time and gym resistance in the same period.

items.note: Only if your shoulders tolerate it
Optional, only if your wrists tolerate it

warm_up.name: Gentle warm-up
warm_up.what: Gets your body warm and moving before the main exercises.
steps: Choose the treadmill (walking) or the exercise bike, whichever feels better today.
Start slowly and settle into a comfortable pace.
You should be able to chat easily the whole time.
tips: Warmer, not tired, is the aim.
modifications: Shorten it if you feel tired before you start.
safety: Hold the treadmill rails to get on and off.
On the bike, set the seat so your knee stays slightly bent.

glute_bridge.name: Glute bridge
glute_bridge.what: Strengthens your bottom (glutes) and the back of your legs, which supports your hips and lower back.
steps: Lie on your back on the mat, knees bent, feet flat and hip-width apart.
Gently tighten your tummy and squeeze your bottom.
Lift your hips a little way off the mat, only as high as feels comfortable.
Pause for a moment, then lower slowly.
tips: A small lift is fine. Control matters more than height.
Breathe out as you lift.
modifications: Put a folded towel under your head if your neck feels tense.
contraindications: Skip it if lying on your back aggravates your neck or back today.
safety: Stop if you feel sharp pain in your back or hips.

hip_abductor.name: Hip abductor (machine)
hip_abductor.what: Strengthens the outer hips and glutes, which help keep your hips and knees steady when you walk.
steps: Choose the lightest weight to start. Ask an instructor to help set up the machine.
Sit back with the pads against the outside of your knees.
Slowly press your knees outwards as far as is comfortable.
Bring them back together slowly, under control.
tips: Slow and smooth both ways.
A small range is fine.
safety: Stop if you feel pinching in the hips.

leg_press.name: Leg press (machine)
leg_press.what: Strengthens your thighs and glutes for everyday things like stairs and getting up from a chair.
steps: Start with a light weight. Ask an instructor to check the seat position.
Sit back with your feet flat on the plate, hip-width apart.
Push the plate away slowly until your legs are almost straight. Don't lock your knees.
Let the plate come back slowly, only as far as feels comfortable.
tips: Keep your back against the seat.
Breathe out as you push.
modifications: Use a shorter range of movement.
contraindications: Skip it if it aggravates your knees today.

abdominal_bracing.name: Abdominal bracing
abdominal_bracing.what: Gently wakes up your deep tummy muscles, which support your back and posture.
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent, or sit tall on a chair.
Breathe in normally.
As you breathe out, gently draw your tummy in, as if bracing for a light tap.
Hold for a few seconds while breathing normally, then relax.
tips: Gentle, about a quarter of your full effort.
Keep breathing, never hold your breath.
modifications: Do it seated if lying down is uncomfortable.
safety: Stop if it causes pain or makes you dizzy.

heel_slides.name: Heel slides
heel_slides.what: Gentle core and hip control, keeping your tummy steady while one leg moves.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Gently brace your tummy as in abdominal bracing.
Slowly slide one heel along the mat until the leg is nearly straight.
Slide it back slowly, then switch legs.
tips: Keep your lower back still and relaxed.
Slow is best.
modifications: Slide only part of the way.
Put a towel under your heel so it glides more easily.
safety: Stop if your back starts to ache.

cool_down.name: Cool-down
cool_down.what: Lets your body settle after the session.
steps: Walk slowly for a couple of minutes.
Do a few gentle stretches that feel nice, such as calves, thighs and shoulders.
Hold each stretch softly. No forcing and no bouncing.
tips: It should feel relaxing.

hamstring_curl.name: Seated hamstring curl (machine)
hamstring_curl.what: Strengthens the back of your thighs, which supports your knees.
steps: Choose the lightest weight. Ask an instructor to set the machine up for you.
Sit with the pad behind your lower legs, just above the ankles.
Slowly bend your knees to pull the pad down and under.
Let it come back up slowly.
tips: Slow and controlled.
Keep your back against the seat.
contraindications: Skip it if it aggravates your knees today.
safety: Stop if you feel cramp or sharp pain.

calf_raise.name: Supported calf raises
equipment: Something steady to hold, or a calf machine
calf_raise.what: Strengthens your calves and ankles for walking and balance.
steps: Stand holding something steady, feet hip-width apart.
Slowly rise up onto your toes.
Pause for a moment, then lower your heels slowly.
tips: Hold on for balance. That's what the support is for.
Small and smooth is fine.
modifications: Do them seated (lift your heels while sitting).
safety: Stop if you feel cramp or ankle pain.

seated_row.name: Seated row (machine)
seated_row.what: Strengthens your upper back for better posture.
steps: Choose the lightest weight. Ask an instructor to check the setup.
Sit tall with your chest towards the pad and hold the handles.
Gently squeeze your shoulder blades back as you pull the handles towards you.
Let them go back slowly.
tips: Shoulders down, away from your ears.
Breathe out as you pull.
contraindications: Only do this if your shoulders tolerate it. Skip it if your shoulders or neck are sore.
safety: Stop if it aggravates your neck or shoulders.

bicep_curl.name: Bicep curls
bicep_curl.what: Strengthens the front of your arms for lifting and carrying.
steps: Sit or stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forwards.
Slowly bend your elbows to bring the weights up.
Lower them slowly.
tips: Keep your elbows by your sides.
Keep your wrists straight.
modifications: Do one arm at a time.
contraindications: Optional. Only do this if your wrists tolerate it.

swim.name: Swim
swim.what: Low-impact movement, with the water supporting your body.
steps: Swim at an easy, comfortable pace.
Take breaks at the side whenever you need to.
Choose a stroke that doesn't bother your neck or shoulders.
Stop before you get exhausted.
tips: Gently walking or floating in the water counts too.
safety: Don't make swims longer until you're recovering well from your current ones.

walk.name: Woodland walk
walk.what: Gentle time outdoors. Optional, and only if it feels good.
steps: Walk at an easy pace.
Turn back whenever you like.
tips: Enjoy it. There's no distance or time to hit.
modifications: A shorter walk, or a sit on a bench, is fine.
safety: Choose even paths if your energy is low.

readiness.method: Enter pain (0-10) and energy (1-5). The app compares them with your usual day, suggests a colour, and you confirm or change it.

amber.label: Amber
amber.meaning: More pain or fatigue than usual
amber.action: Do a lighter version (about half), or rest.

red.label: Red
red.meaning: Flare, significant exhaustion or poor recovery
red.action: Rest. There's nothing to catch up on.

readiness.override: You can always choose rest instead, whatever the colour.

sequence: Get comfortable with the movement and how you recover
Repeat the starting routine when you tolerate it
Only then consider a small increase in resistance
rules: Change one thing at a time.
Wait until the 24 h and 48 h checks are in before deciding a session felt easy.
Don't increase swim time and gym resistance in the same period.
The app only suggests. You decide.

general: Start with light resistance and controlled movements.
Rest between exercises as long as you need.
Avoid pushing through significant pain or fatigue.
Avoid anything that aggravates your wrists, shoulders, neck or knees.
Notice how you feel later that day and over the next 24-48 hours.
Ask a gym instructor to check the machine setup and your technique.
safety.crashes: If activity keeps causing big or long-lasting crashes, reduce activity and talk to a healthcare professional.

nutrition.note: Small, kind habits. No banned foods, no counting.

body.note: Optional. Only if and when you'd like to.

options: Adjust to make it more achievable
Progress gradually if recovery has been good
Prioritise recovery if symptoms have increased
review.success: Success means taking part in a way you can keep up, better everyday function and good recovery, not completing every session.
